title: Use audited material ownership when authorizing material corrections
rationale: The validated item dictionary has evidence_keys and now derives material ownership exclusively from the previous formal evidence directory. Obsolete candidates[member].materials can no longer authorize changing an item supported only by another audited material or expand that item's affected material set. Omissions lack evidence_keys and retain their candidate-source lineage. The new migrated-attribution test passes for both legitimate correction and rejected drift. Independent candidate12 probes accepted omission restoration, item reordering, new directly sourced discovery and retained omission; they rejected protected name, evidence detail, evidence material and other-source ledger drift at merge before review1/history. Exact revision11 plus the new tests independently reproduced the original unauthorized acceptance as an expected post-implementation replay failure.
verification: 142 snapshot-bound direct unit-test invocations PASS, including both new material-attribution parameters
8 independent ownership boundary probes PASS; all four unauthorized-drift cases had zero history queries
revision11 replay: legitimate control PASS; protected-item drift EXPECTED_FAIL
remaining_limits: Formal evidence/source_checks are audited model proposals, not independently proven visual truth.
Shared-source omission and every split/merge combination were not exhaustively verified.
Current-state documentation and actual content acceptance remain open; this disposition is not release or ISS closure.

title: Request-byte telemetry counts the pre-SDK dictionary instead of the transmitted JSON body
rationale: The pre-SDK JSONEncoder estimate is removed. A request-local asynchronous HTTPX event hook reads only len(request.content), after SDK body transformation and serialization. The real-SDK regression with Unicode, an image and extra_body flattening passes. Independent synthetic transport measurement reported and captured exactly 1053 bytes. Nine real-SDK lifecycle probes each sent one request, closed the supplied HTTPX client and transport, and restored both process slots; cancellation and absolute timeout also cancelled the active transport. max_retries=0, stateless store=false, thinking disabled, stage deadlines, token budgets, image/text limits, error mapping and existing safe telemetry consumers remain unchanged. Exact revision11 with the new transport equality test independently reproduced the mismatch as an expected replay failure.
verification: 25 provider direct test invocations PASS as part of the 142-test direct run
9 real-SDK lifecycle probes PASS: success, cancellation, absolute timeout, HTTP timeout, network error,429,500,incomplete response,malformed output
success/incomplete/malformed: captured body and emitted request_bytes both1053; all modes exactly one transport request
remaining_limits: request_bytes measures the last observed serialized HTTP body, not headers,TLS,total redirected traffic or confirmed delivery.
Transport failures/cancellation still do not emit analysis_stage_completed; no failed-attempt byte total is claimed.
No maximum-size/concurrent live SDK memory, real network/model or cloud resource acceptance was run.
